facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: the FY2025 audit-backed statements and the 2026 interim statements with 2025 comparatives give a reported base for the latest twelve months and for each discrete quarter of 2026 from the three-month columns. This supports the data foundation for CP-1 and the business context for CP-1A. - Strongest contrary evidence: the debt and covenant mechanics sit in filing summaries and not in the executed credit agreement or indentures, which are listed only as exhibits (10-K FY2025 page:180: "4.4 Indenture, dated as of February 13, 2020, by and between Centene Corporation, as issuer, and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust"). The risk mechanism is that a consumer may read the issuer's debt-to-capital ratio as a covenant test when the credit agreement's own definition is not available, which would mis-state covenant headroom in CP-2. - Second mechanism: the Part D receivable sale is accounted as a sale, so the receivable leaves the balance sheet and the cash proceeds are operating cash flow (Q3 10-Q page:14: "The cash proceeds and associated loss on sale of receivables are recorded as operating cash flows."). A consumer that reads operating cash flow without this note would overstate organic cash conversion, which CP-1 and CP-2 must separate from the sale. - Third mechanism: the Magellan businesses are held for sale, so segment and consolidated trends include a perimeter that is leaving (Q3 10-Q page:13). CP-1A must keep that perimeter visible. - What cannot proceed: legal interpretation of covenants, baskets or guarantees; guarantor-level or restricted-group analysis; rating-agency or market-based valuation work; any fact after October 27, 2026. - Next evidence action: supply the Credit Agreement dated March 5, 2025 and the indentures (exhibit index, 10-K FY2025 page:180), the Receivable Purchase Agreement and Performance Guaranty (10-K FY2025 page:179), the Magellan sale agreement, any 8-Ks after October 27, 2026, and rating reports if relative-value work is wanted.

This supports the data foundation for CP-1 and the business context for CP-1A.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the debt and covenant mechanics sit in filing summaries and not in the executed credit agreement or indentures, which are listed only as exhibits (10-K FY2025 page:180: "4.4 Indenture, dated as of February 13, 2020, by and between Centene Corporation, as issuer, and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust"). The risk mechanism is that a consumer may read the issuer's debt-to-capital ratio as a covenant test when the credit agreement's own definition is not available, which would mis-state covenant headroom in CP-2.

A consumer that reads operating cash flow without this note would overstate organic cash conversion, which CP-1 and CP-2 must separate from the sale.
- Third mechanism: the Magellan businesses are held for sale, so segment and consolidated trends include a perimeter that is leaving (Q3 10-Q page:13). CP-1A must keep that perimeter visible.

- What cannot proceed: legal interpretation of covenants, baskets or guarantees; guarantor-level or restricted-group analysis; rating-agency or market-based valuation work; any fact after October 27, 2026.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: CENTENE CORP has a usable financial base for downstream work, with stated limits. Audited FY2025 statements and unaudited Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 statements with 2025 comparatives are located and their totals recompute. On the analyst-calculated EBITDA used throughout (the issuer reports none), LTM leverage to September 30, 2026 is 3.62x and LTM cover of cash interest is 6.85x, against 6.86x and 3.92x for FY2025, when the health benefits ratio rose to 91.9% from 88.3% in FY2024. Total debt fell from 17,401 at December 31, 2025 to 15,542 at September 30, 2026 as senior notes were repurchased, and the remaining 2027 notes were redeemed in October 2026. Three cautions control the read. Earnings are front-loaded, so the LTM ratios are better than the third quarter run rate. Consolidated cash is mainly held by regulated subsidiaries, so net debt on that cash would mislead. Operating cash flow is distorted by pass-through timing and the receivable sale.

facts.label: Narrative review
facts.text: - Leverage: total debt fell from 17,401 to 15,542 between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026, and the analyst-calculated LTM ratio is 3.62x against 6.86x for FY2025. Mechanism: the FY2025 ratio was inflated by lower earnings, since the health benefits ratio rose to 91.9% from 88.3% in FY2024 (EBITDA already adds back the impairment), while 2026 repurchases of 1,847 par of the 2027 and 2028 notes reduced the numerator. Implication: leverage has returned toward the FY2024 level of 2.98x but is not yet there, and it rests on an earnings recovery that is not evenly spread across the year. - Earnings shape: calculated EBITDA was 2,568 in Q1 2026, 1,933 in Q2 and 325 in Q3, against 556 in Q3 2025 (C7). The health benefits ratio rose through the year from 87.3% in Q1 to 89.6% in Q2 and 92.7% in Q3 (Q1 10-Q page:32; Q2 10-Q page:37; Q3 10-Q page:40). Implication: the LTM ratio overstates the run rate that the second half implies; the creditor should watch fourth quarter results before treating 3.62x as stable. - Coverage: LTM EBITDA over interest paid is 6.85x against 3.92x for FY2025 and 9.03x for FY2024. Implication: coverage is adequate and improving, helped by lower interest expense (634 LTM against 678 in FY2025). Interest guidance for 2026 of 600 to 620 implies a fourth quarter of 134 to 154 against 466 in nine months (C10). - Cash flow quality: nine-month operating cash flow of 4,287 includes net proceeds of 970 from the March 2026 sale of Part D receivables, which the filing records as operating cash flow ("The cash proceeds and associated loss on sale of receivables are recorded as operating cash flows", Q3 10-Q page:14), and the third quarter shows an operating cash outflow of 3,669 as state pass-through payments of about 4,500 held at June 30, 2026 were paid through. Implication: LTM operating cash flow less capital expenditures of 3,943 is not a recurring free cash flow measure; excluding the 970 gives 2,973 (C11). - Liquidity: consolidated cash is 20,700 but unregulated cash is 376 and the part available for general corporate use is 175. The undrawn revolver of 4,000 has no letters of credit against it. Implication: parent liquidity is 4,175 on the derived measure and depends on the revolver and on subsidiary dividends (1.7 billion in nine months), not on headline cash. The 2027 notes are cleared; the next maturity in the debt register is the 2028 notes of 2,101. - Perimeter and claims: Magellan Health assets and liabilities of 312 each are held for sale (Q3 10-Q page:13), and the Part D receivable program of up to 4,250 is a financing source that sits outside debt. Implication: perimeter and funding-source changes make period comparisons less clean. - Data quality: every recomputed total ties (C5, C6). Known inconsistencies are the 2025 comparative reclassification and the 10-K maturity total (gaps). Source quality is high for filed statements; releases add no independent facts. - Definition risks: EBITDA, net debt and parent liquidity are analyst constructs; the issuer's debt-to-capital ratio is the only leverage metric the issuer prints; the covenant definition is unknown; HBR is issuer-defined. - Key gaps: executed credit agreement and indentures; guarantors; receivable purchase agreement; discrete quarterly cash flow statements; undrawn facility size at December 31, 2024.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: CENTENE CORP is a publicly listed, widely held managed care organization with no sponsor, controlling owner or leveraged transaction in the supplied sources. Its credit-relevant facts are operating and regulatory. Revenue comes mainly from state Medicaid agencies and from the federal government through Medicare and the Marketplace, so margin is the spread between premium set by payors and medical costs, which the issuer measures as the health benefits ratio. Membership of 25,698,200 at September 30, 2026 was below the 27,968,100 of a year earlier, driven by a Marketplace decline, while stand-alone Part D membership grew. The record shows a company that spent 2026 reducing debt, repricing the Marketplace and absorbing severance costs, while facing dated regulatory changes in 2027 and 2028. The corporate transactions in the record are small relative to the group: the pending Magellan Health sale, a receivable sale facility with MUFG Bank, Ltd., and note repurchases. No new debt was issued in 2026. Ownership above the filings, board composition and the terms of the sale and financing agreements are Not supplied, so sponsor behaviour is judged on documented actions only and legal capacity is not assessed.

facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Medicaid was 57% of FY2025 external revenues; Florida and New York are each about 10% or more of Medicaid premium revenues (10-K FY2025 page:13, page:15); the Florida CMS contract concluded and Hawaii contracts were not renewed (Q3 10-Q page:37). Mechanism: premiums and contracts are set by a small number of public payors through rate cycles and procurements, so a single loss or rate shortfall changes revenue and margin quickly. Implication: revenue is large but not locked in; the creditor should weight procurement outcomes and rate adequacy ahead of absolute scale. Countering fact: new and renewed contracts, for example Illinois beginning January 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:37). 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: health benefits ratio of 91.9% for FY2025 against 88.3% for FY2024 and 92.7% in Q3 2026 after 87.3% in Q1 (10-K FY2025 page:107; Q1 10-Q page:32; Q3 10-Q page:40). Mechanism: with medical costs the dominant cost line and premiums fixed for the year, a small ratio drift removes most of the margin, and Medicare costs rise through the year as deductibles are met. Implication: LTM measures in CP-1 are flattering relative to the second half; monitor fourth quarter results and the 2027 rate cycle. Countering fact: the nine-month ratio of 89.9% was better than 91.1% a year earlier (Q3 10-Q page:42). 3. Regulatory and eligibility risk. Evidence: OBBBA work requirements and funding changes, expiry of enhanced Marketplace subsidies and a fall in Medicare Advantage Star Ratings coverage to about 42% of membership in plans rated 3.5 stars or higher from about 60% (Q3 10-Q page:30, page:31, page:38). Mechanism: eligibility and subsidy changes reduce membership and raise morbidity before rates adjust; lower Star Ratings flow into 2028 plan year revenues. Implication: expect membership and revenue pressure through 2027 and 2028 with an uncertain timing of rate offsets. Countering fact: the dual-eligible integration rule from 2030 favours Centene's overlapping Medicaid and Medicare footprint, as management states (Q3 10-Q page:32), which is Management Language. 4. Sponsor alignment and creditor control. Evidence: no sponsor; documented debt reduction and a pause in repurchases (Q3 10-Q page:21, page:46). Mechanism: with dispersed ownership, capital allocation is decided by the board and constrained by covenants not supplied. Implication: documented behaviour is creditor-supportive, but this is not a contractual protection. Counter: the receivable sale facility with repurchase obligations (see conflicts). 5. Key uncertainties. Magellan sale terms and timing; outcome of Texas and Georgia protests; the receivable agreement; covenant definitions; events after October 27, 2026. These are listed in ## Gaps.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: There is no sponsor, acquisition or leveraged buyout in the supplied sources, and no new debt was issued in 2026. The cash flow statement shows no proceeds from long-term debt in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, against 750 in the same period of 2025 (CP-1). The transactions that matter to a creditor are three. First, the pending sale of the remaining Magellan Health businesses, agreed in December 2025: its buyer, price, expected closing date and use of proceeds are Not supplied, and held-for-sale assets and liabilities of 312 each are on the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. Second, the February 13, 2026 master receivable purchase agreement with MUFG Bank, Ltd. for up to 4,250 of 2025 plan year stand-alone Part D risk-sharing receivables: a participating interest of 1,000 was sold in March 2026 for net proceeds of 970, which funded part of the redemption of the 2027 notes, with 3,250 of purchase capacity remaining at September 30, 2026 and settlement of the sold interest expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Third, debt reduction through the senior note repurchase program, whose authorization was raised in February, May and October 2026, and the October 2026 redemption in full of the remaining 569 of 2027 notes; this is a subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. The credit agreement dated March 5, 2025, with a revolver of 4,000 and a term loan, is described in the 2026 filings without any amendment. The next scheduled note maturity on the debt register in CP-1 is the 2028 notes. Terms of the agreements are Not supplied, so legal capacity, baskets and covenants are not assessed here.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Centene is a large, government-funded health insurer whose credit quality improved in 2026 but remains sensitive to medical costs and regulation. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt fell to USD 15,542 million from USD 17,401 million, calculated leverage on last-twelve-month EBITDA is 3.62x against 6.86x for FY2025, and a USD 4,000 million revolver is undrawn. The weakest point is earnings stability and parent-level cash: calculated EBITDA was USD 2,568 million in Q1 2026 but USD 325 million in Q3 2026, and cash available for general corporate use was USD 175 million. What decides the outcome is whether the health benefits ratio holds through the fourth quarter and the 2027 rate cycle while Marketplace, Medicaid and Star Ratings changes take effect.

facts.label: Credit assessment
facts.text: Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): Centene has repaired its balance sheet faster than its earnings are proven, so the credit is improving but depends on a stable health benefits ratio and on rate and regulatory outcomes that are outside its control. Basis: CP-1 leverage and quarterly EBITDA shape; CP-1A Credit translations.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, Centene has reduced debt materially: total debt was USD 15,542 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 17,401 million at December 31, 2025, the 2027 notes, carried at USD 2,211 million at year-end, fell to USD 568 million at September 30, 2026, and the remainder was redeemed in October 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Debt register, Chart data: debt maturities; CP-1A Timeline). The mechanism is note repurchases funded by cash and by a USD 970 million receivable sale, and the implication is that no scheduled note maturity falls before 2028 on the CP-1 register.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, leverage looks sound on last-twelve-month figures but less so on the quarterly shape. Calculated total debt over EBITDA is 3.62x, against 2.98x for FY2024 and 6.86x for FY2025, and EBITDA over cash interest paid is 6.85x (Analyst Interpretation on an analyst-defined EBITDA; CP-1 Chart data: leverage and interest cover). Calculated EBITDA was USD 2,568 million in Q1 2026, USD 1,933 million in Q2 2026 and USD 325 million in Q3 2026, and Medicare Advantage earnings are front-loaded by the issuer's own account (Management Language; CP-1A Company and operating model, Seasonality). A creditor should therefore treat 3.62x as a ceiling on comfort until fourth quarter results confirm the recovery.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, parent liquidity is the binding constraint. Consolidated cash of USD 20,700 million sits mostly in regulated subsidiaries, unregulated cash is USD 376 million, and USD 175 million is available for general corporate use; management expects only about USD 20 million of net insurance-subsidiary dividends for the rest of 2026 (Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026; CP-1A Company and operating model, Subsidiary dividends). Debt service therefore rests on the undrawn USD 4,000 million revolver and on dividend capacity that state regulators control, with interest paid of USD 627 million over the last twelve months.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, reported cash flow overstates recurring generation. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 4,287 million includes net receivable sale proceeds of USD 970 million, and Q3 2026 operating cash flow was an outflow as state pass-through payments were paid through (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Reported cash flows, Narrative review). Free cash flow of USD 3,943 million over the last twelve months should not be read as a recurring figure.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fifth, business risk is driven by government payors and dated regulatory change. Medicaid was 57% of FY2025 external revenues, Florida and New York each exceed about 10% of Medicaid premium revenues, certain Hawaii Medicaid contracts and the Florida Children's Medical Services contract were lost, and Texas and Georgia protests are open (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model, Concentration and Contract renewal risk). Marketplace membership fell to 3,403,300 from 5,828,100, 2027 Star Ratings cover about 42% of Medicare Advantage membership at 3.5 stars or higher against about 60%, and California and Medicaid work-requirement changes take effect in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Timeline, Credit translations). Revenue and margin visibility into 2027 and 2028 is therefore lower than the 2026 recovery suggests.

facts.text: Sixth, the covenant has wide stated room but cannot be verified. Issuer debt to capital is 41.1% against a 0.60 to 1.00 maximum, and the issuer states compliance (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Covenants as disclosed), but the agreement's definition, guarantors and any restrictions on distributions are not supplied, so covenant headroom is Not calculable and legal capacity is not assessed (Insufficient Information).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Scale and diversification across Medicaid, Medicare, Commercial and Other, with Medicaid in 30 states and Medicare Advantage in 32 states, spreads exposure across many payors even though two states are material (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company profile, Company and operating model). Deleveraging is real and documented: debt of USD 15,542 million, debt to capital of 41.1% against 46.5% at December 31, 2025, and the 2027 notes cleared (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Reported balance sheet, Debt register). Liquidity at the parent is supported by an undrawn USD 4,000 million revolver with no letters of credit against it, maturing March 5, 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026). Interest cover has recovered to 6.85x from 3.92x on an analyst-defined EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Chart data: interest cover). Documented management behaviour is creditor-supportive, with note repurchases, no common stock repurchases in Q3 2026, no sponsor and no documented value extraction (Analyst Interpretation on documented actions; CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour). The medical cost position improved on a nine-month basis, with a health benefits ratio of 89.9% against 91.1% a year earlier (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Credit translations).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Earnings are volatile and front-loaded: calculated EBITDA fell to USD 2,535 million in FY2025 from USD 6,213 million in FY2024, and was USD 325 million in Q3 2026 (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics, Narrative review). Parent cash is thin relative to USD 15,542 million of debt, and upstream dividends are regulator-controlled (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026). The business depends on government rate setting and procurement, with dated headwinds in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model, Timeline). Cash flow is distorted by pass-through timing and a receivable sale that carries repurchase obligations under the agreement, which is not supplied (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information; CP-1A Conflicts logged). Documentation gaps limit the view: covenant definitions, indentures, guarantors and the Magellan sale agreement are Not supplied (Insufficient Information). A Securities Action alleging false statements about 2025 guidance is pending, with no loss estimate and accrued amounts described as not material (Management Language; CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour).

spans.text: # CP-0 Source readiness: CENTENE CORP (cnc)
## Request

- Issuer: CENTENE CORP (issuer id `cnc`), registrant name "CENTENE CORPORATION", ticker CNC. As-of date and information cutoff: 2026-11-05. Reporting currency: USD. Current period q3-2026, prior period fy-2025 (context).
- Run `cnc-2026-11-05-credit_snapshot-host`, pathway `credit_snapshot`. Requested downstream modules: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 (the launcher's `minimum` set). CP-0 runs first as their dependency.
- Execution: host session. The host read the pinned files and wrote this answer. No provider was called.
- Question: can the supplied public filings and releases support CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, and what remains blocked?

- Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. This answer gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it normalizes, reconciles and calculates nothing.
- Locators are `page:N` chunk numbers of the pinned `.jsonl` extracts, not printed page numbers. Quotes are copied from the cited chunk.
## Sources

### Supplied handoffs
None. CP-0 is the first module, so no upstream handoff exists.
### Provenance note

The first chunk of each extract begins "Visible text of ..." and names the sha256 of the original HTML document. Those original-document hashes (10-K FY2025 84f363689f1eece5286ce0dc59aa3056b86661579db8f8deb3c84c222eb50ec3; Q1 10-Q ca7706752a9c72356443db182cb1fb91c3cae7866d206d7a26e6c3eb7ad81d66; Q2 10-Q 7fc98f7d77f2e49ceaa9d2468247189c3993bb785908f54fb145bfc7c86f2918; Q3 10-Q 79ddcf084bbb94a972eaff9b37bfae2e01e530497d998523788ec4a726b43a76) differ from the pinned extract hashes above, as expected. The pinned extract hashes are the ones this run is bound to. The original HTML and XBRL are not supplied.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven supplied filings and releases are sufficient for all four downstream modules to run, each with stated limitations. No consumer is blocked or conditional. | Medium | Executed credit agreement, indentures, receivable purchase agreement and divestiture agreement are not supplied; sources are text extracts without original tables or XBRL. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Audited annual statements and unaudited statements for every 2026 quarter are present, with comparatives. | Supports reported-fact extraction and trend work; cash flows are cumulative only, so quarterly flows must be derived downstream. | High |

| Debt, covenant, letter of credit and liquidity disclosures are located in each filing, including the October senior note redemption. | Debt and headroom analysis can proceed from filed notes, but covenant terms rest on summaries, not executed agreements. | Medium |

| The receivable sale arrangement and the pending Magellan divestiture are described only in filing notes. | Off-balance-sheet liquidity support and perimeter changes cannot be checked against contracts; treat them as disclosed claims. | Medium |

| The releases are management documents that repeat the filings. No rating reports, investor decks or market data are supplied. | Releases add no independent corroboration; rating and relative-value judgments have no source support in this set. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with bounded limitations. All four consumers, CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, are READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, and none is conditional or blocked. The set holds one audited annual report for FY2025 with FY2024 and FY2023 comparatives, three unaudited quarterly reports for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 with 2025 comparatives, and three earnings releases dated 2026-04-28, 2026-07-28 and 2026-10-27. All of it is dated before the cutoff of 2026-11-05. The main restrictions are that the filed financial statements are the controlling evidence, the releases are secondary and largely duplicative, and no executed financing, receivable-sale or divestiture agreements are supplied. Command sheet: CP-1 RUN; CP-1A RUN; CP-2 RUN; CP-5 RUN.
### Consumer assessments
| Consumer | Status | Basis | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Audited FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 statements (10-K FY2025 page:129, page:131) and unaudited Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 statements with 2025 comparatives (Q1 10-Q page:7, Q2 10-Q page:7, Q3 10-Q page:8) are located, with debt notes in all four filings. | Cash flow statements are cumulative (three, six and nine months), so discrete quarterly cash flow is not printed. Text extracts flatten tables. Segment, KPI and non-GAAP tables sit in the 10-Qs and releases. |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business, segments, regulatory and contract changes, the pending Magellan sale, the receivable sale arrangement and management narrative are located in 10-K FY2025 page:12 onward, Q3 10-Q page:28 to page:39 and the releases. | Magellan sale agreement, receivable purchase agreement and contract-award documents are not supplied. No proxy statement, no investor presentation. |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | CP-2 synthesises from CP-1 and CP-1A. Covenant, liquidity, letter of credit and unregulated cash text is located (Q3 10-Q page:46, page:47). | Covenant definitions are known only from filing summaries. No ratings, market prices or peer data are supplied (context). |

| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every source has stable chunk numbers, so claims can be traced to a locator and quote. | Visual and table-layout checks against the filed HTML are not possible. Releases cannot corroborate filings. |
### Source register

- Family and authority: filed annual report on Form 10-K (10-K FY2025 page:1: "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025"). Original authority for audited consolidated statements, notes and Item 7 text. Auditor report signed KPMG LLP in St. Louis (10-K FY2025 page:129: "We have served as the Company's auditor since 2005.").

- Entity and perimeter: Centene Corporation and subsidiaries, consolidated. Parent-company-only condensed information is also supplied (10-K FY2025 page:170: "20. Condensed Financial Information of Registrant").

- Period and basis: FY2025 with FY2024 comparatives on the balance sheet and FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 on operations and cash flows. US GAAP, USD millions (10-K FY2025 page:129: "CONSOLIDATED BALANCE SHEETS (In millions, except shares in thousands and per share data in dollars)").

- Located content: balance sheet and operations statement (page:129), cash flows with cash paid for interest and taxes (page:131, page:132), debt note (page:158 to page:160), leases (page:160), segment note (page:169, page:170), parent-only schedule (page:170 to page:172), Item 9B on the receivable purchase agreement (page:177) and exhibit index (page:179 to page:182).

- Version relation: the base annual report for the period. The Q3 10-Q balance sheet carries the 2025 year-end comparative and states that "Certain 2025 amounts in the consolidated financial statements and notes to the consolidated financial statements have been reclassified to conform to the 2026 presentation." (Q3 10-Q page:12). Where the 10-K and a later 10-Q differ on a 2025 figure, both are kept and CP-1 must label which presentation it uses.

- Family and authority: filed quarterly reports with unaudited statements (Q1 10-Q page:1: "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026"; Q2 10-Q page:1: "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026"; Q3 10-Q page:1: "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026"). Signed as of April 28, 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:42), July 28, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:49) and October 27, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:52: "duly authorized as of October 27, 2026").
- Entity and perimeter: Centene Corporation and subsidiaries, consolidated (Q3 10-Q page:1: "CENTENE CORPORATION (Exact name of registrant as specified in its charter)").

- Period and basis: three-month columns for each quarter and cumulative columns (three, six, nine months) with 2025 comparatives; balance sheets compare to December 31, 2025. USD millions (Q3 10-Q page:8: "CONSOLIDATED BALANCE SHEETS (In millions, except shares in thousands and per share data in dollars)").

- Located content in the Q3 10-Q: balance sheet (page:8), operations (page:9), cash flows with interest paid and taxes paid (page:11), debt note (page:20, page:21), the receivable sale note (page:14, page:15), segment note (page:22 to page:24), legal matters (page:25 to page:27), MD&A (page:28 to page:50) and unregulated cash (page:46).

- Version relation: each 10-Q supersedes nothing; the three remain separate active sources. Q2 and Q3 interim data build on each other: the Q3 10-Q states "the quarter-to-date operating cash flow use of $3,669 million" (Q3 10-Q page:12), which matches the Q3 release (Q3 release page:1: "Total cash flow (used in) operations (in millions) $ (3,669)").
#### Q1 release, Q2 release and Q3 release

- Family and authority: issuer news releases furnished as Exhibit 99.1, dated April 28, 2026, July 28, 2026 and October 27, 2026 (Q3 release page:1: "ST. LOUIS, October 27, 2026 -- Centene Corporation (NYSE: CNC)"). Management-prepared, unaudited; they carry attributed management narrative and non-GAAP measures.

- Located content: reported and adjusted results, reconciliations, guidance (Q3 release page:4), statements of operations, balance sheet and cash flows (Q3 release page:12, page:13), membership, medical claims liability roll-forward (Q3 release page:15) and a liquidity statement (Q3 release page:3: "maintained $175 million of cash available for general corporate use").

- Version relation: their statements repeat the 10-Q statements for the same date, so the 10-Q controls and the release is not independent corroboration. The release also states "Debt reduced by $1.1 billion since June 30, 2026" (Q3 release page:1), a management claim that sits on top of the filed debt note.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Centene Corporation, Delaware, NYSE "CNC" (Q3 10-Q page:1: "Common Stock $0.001 Par Value CNC New York Stock Exchange"). The same entity files the 10-K, three 10-Qs and three releases. Identity is confirmed from content, not file names.

- Debt issuer and borrower: Centene Corporation issues the senior notes ("The indentures governing the senior notes listed in the table above contain restrictive covenants of Centene Corporation." 10-K FY2025 page:158). The Revolving Credit Facility and Term Loan Facility sit under one credit agreement (10-K FY2025 page:159: "The maturity date for the New Credit Agreement is March 5, 2030.").

- Guarantors and restricted group: no subsidiary guarantor of the notes or the credit agreement is named in any supplied source (a text search of the 10-K FY2025 for "guarant" finds no guarantor of the notes or the credit agreement; the hits are generic risk language, government-backed securities and the performance guaranty on the receivable purchase agreement, page:177). The context leaves guarantors blank. Guarantor-level analysis is an unresolved distinction and a gap, not evidence of absence.

- Operating subsidiaries: health plans are regulated entities that are subject to statutory capital rules (10-K FY2025 page:33), and the filings split cash and investments into regulated and unregulated (Q3 release page:14). Parent-only data are supplied only for FY2025 (10-K FY2025 page:170 to page:172).

- Perimeter changes: the remaining Magellan Health businesses are held for sale (Q3 10-Q page:13: "In December 2025, the Company signed a definitive agreement to sell the remaining Magellan Health businesses, which is included in the Other segment."). The 10-K FY2025 also records the earlier Circle Health sale agreement (page:147).
- Currency and units: USD millions except shares in thousands and per share data in dollars. Membership is a count of members. No foreign-currency reporting basis was found.
### Debt, covenant and liquidity coverage

- Debt table at each date: seven senior note series plus a Term Loan Facility and issuance costs (Q3 10-Q page:20: "Total debt 15,542 17,401"; 10-K FY2025 page:158: "Total debt 17,401 18,533"). The Dec 31, 2025 total debt in the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q comparative show the same printed figure.

- Subsequent debt event: "In October 2026, the Company redeemed in full at par the remaining $569 million of its par value Senior Notes due 2027 through the debt repurchase program." (Q3 10-Q page:21). It is dated after the balance sheet date and before the cutoff.

- Covenant: "Our maximum debt-to-capital ratio under the credit agreement may not exceed 0.60 to 1.00." (Q3 10-Q page:47); the 10-K adds a step-up (10-K FY2025 page:159: "to 0.65 to 1.00"). The reported ratio is stated by the issuer (Q3 10-Q page:47: "was 41.1%, compared to 46.5% at December 31, 2025"). The credit agreement definition is not supplied.
- Letters of credit and surety bonds: "We had outstanding letters of credit of $113 million as of September 30, 2026, which were not part of our Revolving Credit Facility." (Q3 10-Q page:47).

- Liquidity: unregulated cash of "$175 million was available for general corporate use at September 30, 2026" (Q3 10-Q page:46). Cash available for general corporate use is also stated for the earlier quarters (Q1 release page:4: "$437 million of cash available for general corporate use"; Q2 release page:3: "$715 million of cash available for general corporate use"). The undrawn revolver amount is not printed as a figure; the 10-Q gives the facility size and "no borrowings outstanding under our Revolving Credit Facility" (Q3 10-Q page:47).

- Receivable sale: "The maximum outstanding purchase amount permitted under the agreement is $4,250 million." (Q3 10-Q page:14). The agreement itself is not supplied; the 10-K FY2025 lists it as Exhibit 2.1 filed with that report (page:179).
- Cash paid: "Interest paid $ 438 $ 458" and "Income taxes paid, net $ 15 $ 540" are the nine-month figures (Q3 10-Q page:11). Annual figures are in 10-K FY2025 page:132.
### Cross-source relationships and conflicts

- No contradiction was found between the 10-K FY2025 year-end balance sheet figures and the December 31, 2025 columns of the Q1 10-Q and Q3 10-Q for total debt, long-term debt and total stockholders' equity. The 2026 10-Qs state that some 2025 amounts were reclassified (Q3 10-Q page:12), so a 2025 comparative can differ from the original 10-K and must be traced to the right document.

- The 10-K FY2025 maturity schedule prints "Total $ 17,493" (page:160). The debt table prints "Total senior notes 15,490" and "Term Loan Facility 2,000" (page:158). The printed schedule total is not identical to the sum of those two lines. This is carried to CP-1 as an unreconciled presentation difference, not resolved here.
- Letters of credit were $120 million at December 31, 2025 (10-K FY2025 page:160) and $113 million at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:47). These are different dates, not a conflict.

- Q3 10-Q page:12 states about $1,635 million of state pass-through payments at September 30, 2026 against about $4,500 million at June 30, 2026. These are balance-sheet timing items that affect quarterly operating cash flow; CP-1 must not read the quarterly cash flow without them.
### Information-availability boundary

- Every source is dated on or before October 27, 2026, which is before the cutoff of 2026-11-05. The latest dated facts are the Q3 10-Q signature and the debt repurchase program balance "as of October 27, 2026" (Q3 10-Q page:21).

- The Q3 10-Q extract does not print the EDGAR filing date, only the signature date, so the filing date is Not supplied. No supplied source dated after October 27, 2026 exists. Events between October 27, 2026 and the as-of date are Not supplied, not absent.
- A digital audio playback of the Q3 call is dated "November 3, 2026" (Q3 release page:4); it is a future logistic date inside a release, not a fact used.
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: the FY2025 audit-backed statements and the 2026 interim statements with 2025 comparatives give a reported base for the latest twelve months and for each discrete quarter of 2026 from the three-month columns. This supports the data foundation for CP-1 and the business context for CP-1A.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the debt and covenant mechanics sit in filing summaries and not in the executed credit agreement or indentures, which are listed only as exhibits (10-K FY2025 page:180: "4.4 Indenture, dated as of February 13, 2020, by and between Centene Corporation, as issuer, and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust"). The risk mechanism is that a consumer may read the issuer's debt-to-capital ratio as a covenant test when the credit agreement's own definition is not available, which would mis-state covenant headroom in CP-2.

- Second mechanism: the Part D receivable sale is accounted as a sale, so the receivable leaves the balance sheet and the cash proceeds are operating cash flow (Q3 10-Q page:14: "The cash proceeds and associated loss on sale of receivables are recorded as operating cash flows."). A consumer that reads operating cash flow without this note would overstate organic cash conversion, which CP-1 and CP-2 must separate from the sale.
- Third mechanism: the Magellan businesses are held for sale, so segment and consolidated trends include a perimeter that is leaving (Q3 10-Q page:13). CP-1A must keep that perimeter visible.

- What cannot proceed: legal interpretation of covenants, baskets or guarantees; guarantor-level or restricted-group analysis; rating-agency or market-based valuation work; any fact after October 27, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply the Credit Agreement dated March 5, 2025 and the indentures (exhibit index, 10-K FY2025 page:180), the Receivable Purchase Agreement and Performance Guaranty (10-K FY2025 page:179), the Magellan sale agreement, any 8-Ks after October 27, 2026, and rating reports if relative-value work is wanted.
## Calculations

No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Every figure above is quoted from a located chunk and is labelled with its period. Where this answer says two printed figures are not identical (the maturity schedule total against the debt table), it leaves the reconciliation to CP-1.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| Credit agreement and indentures not supplied; covenant definitions and guarantor structure unknown | High for legal work; Medium for CP-2 | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the executed Credit Agreement and indentures |
| Receivable Purchase Agreement and Performance Guaranty not supplied; purchaser appetite and terms only from filing notes | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Supply Exhibits 2.1 and 2.2 to the 10-K |
| Magellan sale agreement not supplied; closing terms and proceeds not in the set | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the agreement or the related 8-K |
| Cash flows only cumulative; discrete Q2 and Q3 cash flows are not printed (the Q3 operating figure is quoted) | Medium | CP-1 | Derive downstream from cumulative columns and show the formula |
| Parent-only financial information supplied for FY2025 only | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Treat parent liquidity as annual; do not extend to 2026 |
| Undrawn revolver amount not printed as a figure | Low | CP-2 | Derive from the facility size and borrowings, citing each; the filings state that the letters of credit are not part of the revolver |
| Maturity schedule total differs from the debt table lines (10-K FY2025 page:160 against page:158) | Low | CP-1 | Reconcile in CP-1 and state the choice |
| 2025 comparatives reclassified in 2026 filings | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Label which presentation each 2025 figure uses |
| Events after October 27, 2026 and the Q3 10-Q filing date not supplied | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply later 8-Ks or confirm none |
| No rating reports, investor presentations, market prices or peers | Low for the selected modules | CP-2 | Not required for this scope; keep Not supplied |
| Text extracts only; original HTML tables and XBRL not supplied | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Check flagged tables against the filed HTML |
## Next module

- CP-1: treat the 10-K FY2025 and the 10-Qs as controlling and the releases as secondary. Keep annual, three-month, six-month and nine-month columns separate. Show debt table lines, the October 2026 redemption and the receivable sale as separate items. Label the issuer's debt-to-capital and adjusted measures as issuer-defined.

- CP-1A: carry the Magellan sale, the receivable sale arrangement, the 2026 contract and membership changes and the CMS Star Ratings disclosure as dated facts, and mark anything after October 27, 2026 as Not supplied.
- CP-2 and CP-5: carry the missing executed agreements, the guarantor gap and the cumulative cash flow limitation as restrictions. CP-5 must treat the releases as duplicative of the filings.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Calculated leverage improved sharply from FY2025 as senior notes were repurchased and earnings recovered, but earnings are front-loaded and headline cash is mostly regulated. Parent liquidity rests on a small cash balance and the undrawn revolver. | Medium | The issuer reports no EBITDA, so every leverage and cover ratio uses an analyst definition; covenant definitions and executed agreements are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Calculated leverage on LTM EBITDA is 3.62x, down from 6.86x in FY2025, while total debt fell to 15,542. | Deleveraging is real, but third quarter EBITDA was far below the first two quarters, so the LTM figure flatters the run rate. | Medium |

| Consolidated cash of 20,700 sits mostly in regulated subsidiaries; cash available for general corporate use was 175. | Parent debt service relies on subsidiary dividends and the undrawn 4,000 revolver rather than headline cash. | High |

| Operating cash flow includes state pass-through timing and a 970 net receivable sale in the first quarter. | Reported free cash flow overstates recurring cash generation, and quarterly cash flow is volatile. | Medium |

| Issuer debt-to-capital is 41.1% against a 0.60 maximum, and the 2027 notes were fully redeemed in October 2026. | The nearest maturity is cleared and the stated covenant has wide room, though its definition is unverified. | Medium |
### Financial base view

CENTENE CORP has a usable financial base for downstream work, with stated limits. Audited FY2025 statements and unaudited Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 statements with 2025 comparatives are located and their totals recompute. On the analyst-calculated EBITDA used throughout (the issuer reports none), LTM leverage to September 30, 2026 is 3.62x and LTM cover of cash interest is 6.85x, against 6.86x and 3.92x for FY2025, when the health benefits ratio rose to 91.9% from 88.3% in FY2024. Total debt fell from 17,401 at December 31, 2025 to 15,542 at September 30, 2026 as senior notes were repurchased, and the remaining 2027 notes were redeemed in October 2026. Three cautions control the read. Earnings are front-loaded, so the LTM ratios are better than the third quarter run rate. Consolidated cash is mainly held by regulated subsidiaries, so net debt on that cash would mislead. Operating cash flow is distorted by pass-through timing and the receivable sale.

The issuer reports no EBITDA or Adjusted EBITDA in any supplied source (a text search of all seven sources for "EBITDA" returns nothing). GAAP diluted EPS was a loss of 0.14 in Q3 2026 and earnings of 5.15 for nine months (Q3 10-Q page:9). Adjusted EPS excludes severance and enterprise optimization costs. The Q3 10-Q states severance and third-party vendor costs of 297 in the quarter and 358 in nine months included in selling, general and administrative expenses (Q3 10-Q page:26). ### Narrative review

- Leverage: total debt fell from 17,401 to 15,542 between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026, and the analyst-calculated LTM ratio is 3.62x against 6.86x for FY2025. Mechanism: the FY2025 ratio was inflated by lower earnings, since the health benefits ratio rose to 91.9% from 88.3% in FY2024 (EBITDA already adds back the impairment), while 2026 repurchases of 1,847 par of the 2027 and 2028 notes reduced the numerator. Implication: leverage has returned toward the FY2024 level of 2.98x but is not yet there, and it rests on an earnings recovery that is not evenly spread across the year.

- Earnings shape: calculated EBITDA was 2,568 in Q1 2026, 1,933 in Q2 and 325 in Q3, against 556 in Q3 2025 (C7). The health benefits ratio rose through the year from 87.3% in Q1 to 89.6% in Q2 and 92.7% in Q3 (Q1 10-Q page:32; Q2 10-Q page:37; Q3 10-Q page:40). Implication: the LTM ratio overstates the run rate that the second half implies; the creditor should watch fourth quarter results before treating 3.62x as stable.

- Coverage: LTM EBITDA over interest paid is 6.85x against 3.92x for FY2025 and 9.03x for FY2024. Implication: coverage is adequate and improving, helped by lower interest expense (634 LTM against 678 in FY2025). Interest guidance for 2026 of 600 to 620 implies a fourth quarter of 134 to 154 against 466 in nine months (C10).

- Cash flow quality: nine-month operating cash flow of 4,287 includes net proceeds of 970 from the March 2026 sale of Part D receivables, which the filing records as operating cash flow ("The cash proceeds and associated loss on sale of receivables are recorded as operating cash flows", Q3 10-Q page:14), and the third quarter shows an operating cash outflow of 3,669 as state pass-through payments of about 4,500 held at June 30, 2026 were paid through. Implication: LTM operating cash flow less capital expenditures of 3,943 is not a recurring free cash flow measure; excluding the 970 gives 2,973 (C11).

- Liquidity: consolidated cash is 20,700 but unregulated cash is 376 and the part available for general corporate use is 175. The undrawn revolver of 4,000 has no letters of credit against it. Implication: parent liquidity is 4,175 on the derived measure and depends on the revolver and on subsidiary dividends (1.7 billion in nine months), not on headline cash. The 2027 notes are cleared; the next maturity in the debt register is the 2028 notes of 2,101.

- Perimeter and claims: Magellan Health assets and liabilities of 312 each are held for sale (Q3 10-Q page:13), and the Part D receivable program of up to 4,250 is a financing source that sits outside debt. Implication: perimeter and funding-source changes make period comparisons less clean.

- Data quality: every recomputed total ties (C5, C6). Known inconsistencies are the 2025 comparative reclassification and the 10-K maturity total (gaps). Source quality is high for filed statements; releases add no independent facts.

- Definition risks: EBITDA, net debt and parent liquidity are analyst constructs; the issuer's debt-to-capital ratio is the only leverage metric the issuer prints; the covenant definition is unknown; HBR is issuer-defined.
- Key gaps: executed credit agreement and indentures; guarantors; receivable purchase agreement; discrete quarterly cash flow statements; undrawn facility size at December 31, 2024.

### Business and transaction view

CENTENE CORP is a publicly listed, widely held managed care organization with no sponsor, controlling owner or leveraged transaction in the supplied sources. Its credit-relevant facts are operating and regulatory. Revenue comes mainly from state Medicaid agencies and from the federal government through Medicare and the Marketplace, so margin is the spread between premium set by payors and medical costs, which the issuer measures as the health benefits ratio. Membership of 25,698,200 at September 30, 2026 was below the 27,968,100 of a year earlier, driven by a Marketplace decline, while stand-alone Part D membership grew. The record shows a company that spent 2026 reducing debt, repricing the Marketplace and absorbing severance costs, while facing dated regulatory changes in 2027 and 2028. The corporate transactions in the record are small relative to the group: the pending Magellan Health sale, a receivable sale facility with MUFG Bank, Ltd., and note repurchases. No new debt was issued in 2026. Ownership above the filings, board composition and the terms of the sale and financing agreements are Not supplied, so sponsor behaviour is judged on documented actions only and legal capacity is not assessed.

- Deleveraging and divestitures: since 2022 the record shows divestitures (Magellan Rx, Circle Health, Collaborative Health Systems) and a pending Magellan Health sale, and debt reduction in 2026. Mechanism: asset sales and note repurchases reduce debt and the Other segment's perimeter; proceeds and terms of the pending Magellan sale are Not supplied.
- Acquisitions: no acquisition is documented in 2026. The record does not support an inference about acquisition appetite.

- Monitoring documents the source set lacks: debt schedule by instrument at par (carrying amounts only), covenant certificate and definitions, add-back bridge (the issuer reports no EBITDA), the proxy statement, and the receivable and divestiture agreements. Severity: High for covenant definitions; Medium for the others.
### Conflicts logged
| Topic | Source A | Source B | Effect |

| 2025 risk adjustment benefit recognized in 2026 | "the net pre-tax benefit recognized was $481 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026" (Q2 10-Q page:18) | "the net pre-tax benefit recognized was $480 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026" (Q3 10-Q page:20) | The cumulative benefit appears one lower after a further quarter; not reconciled here. | Medicare and Medicaid membership comparability | Medicare Advantage membership includes integrated plans as a result of the CMS transition in 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:39) | Medicare-Medicaid Plan members are shown in High Acuity Medicaid through December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:38) | Segment membership is not like-for-like across the year-end; a year-on-year change in either line mixes a reclassification with real change |
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Medicaid was 57% of FY2025 external revenues; Florida and New York are each about 10% or more of Medicaid premium revenues (10-K FY2025 page:13, page:15); the Florida CMS contract concluded and Hawaii contracts were not renewed (Q3 10-Q page:37). Mechanism: premiums and contracts are set by a small number of public payors through rate cycles and procurements, so a single loss or rate shortfall changes revenue and margin quickly. Implication: revenue is large but not locked in; the creditor should weight procurement outcomes and rate adequacy ahead of absolute scale. Countering fact: new and renewed contracts, for example Illinois beginning January 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:37).

2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: health benefits ratio of 91.9% for FY2025 against 88.3% for FY2024 and 92.7% in Q3 2026 after 87.3% in Q1 (10-K FY2025 page:107; Q1 10-Q page:32; Q3 10-Q page:40). Mechanism: with medical costs the dominant cost line and premiums fixed for the year, a small ratio drift removes most of the margin, and Medicare costs rise through the year as deductibles are met. Implication: LTM measures in CP-1 are flattering relative to the second half; monitor fourth quarter results and the 2027 rate cycle. Countering fact: the nine-month ratio of 89.9% was better than 91.1% a year earlier (Q3 10-Q page:42).

3. Regulatory and eligibility risk. Evidence: OBBBA work requirements and funding changes, expiry of enhanced Marketplace subsidies and a fall in Medicare Advantage Star Ratings coverage to about 42% of membership in plans rated 3.5 stars or higher from about 60% (Q3 10-Q page:30, page:31, page:38). Mechanism: eligibility and subsidy changes reduce membership and raise morbidity before rates adjust; lower Star Ratings flow into 2028 plan year revenues. Implication: expect membership and revenue pressure through 2027 and 2028 with an uncertain timing of rate offsets. Countering fact: the dual-eligible integration rule from 2030 favours Centene's overlapping Medicaid and Medicare footprint, as management states (Q3 10-Q page:32), which is Management Language.

4. Sponsor alignment and creditor control. Evidence: no sponsor; documented debt reduction and a pause in repurchases (Q3 10-Q page:21, page:46). Mechanism: with dispersed ownership, capital allocation is decided by the board and constrained by covenants not supplied. Implication: documented behaviour is creditor-supportive, but this is not a contractual protection. Counter: the receivable sale facility with repurchase obligations (see conflicts).

5. Key uncertainties. Magellan sale terms and timing; outcome of Texas and Georgia protests; the receivable agreement; covenant definitions; events after October 27, 2026. These are listed in `## Gaps`.
### Consumer assessments
| Consumer | Readiness | What to take from CP-1A | Why it matters | Gap | Required action |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Segment and state concentration, dated regulatory headwinds, the receivable sale and Magellan perimeter, documented deleveraging, no sponsor | Business risk and revenue visibility drive the fundamental credit view | Proxy, agreements and procurement outcomes not supplied | Treat conclusions as based on filings only; carry the conflicts and gaps |

| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every row has a locator and a category; subsequent and future-dated events are labelled | Evidence trace depends on locators and on respecting dates | Releases duplicate filings; the proxy is not supplied | Check figures against CP-1 values and keep Management Language labelled |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no sponsor, acquisition or leveraged buyout in the supplied sources, and no new debt was issued in 2026. The cash flow statement shows no proceeds from long-term debt in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, against 750 in the same period of 2025 (CP-1). The transactions that matter to a creditor are three. First, the pending sale of the remaining Magellan Health businesses, agreed in December 2025: its buyer, price, expected closing date and use of proceeds are Not supplied, and held-for-sale assets and liabilities of 312 each are on the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. Second, the February 13, 2026 master receivable purchase agreement with MUFG Bank, Ltd. for up to 4,250 of 2025 plan year stand-alone Part D risk-sharing receivables: a participating interest of 1,000 was sold in March 2026 for net proceeds of 970, which funded part of the redemption of the 2027 notes, with 3,250 of purchase capacity remaining at September 30, 2026 and settlement of the sold interest expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Third, debt reduction through the senior note repurchase program, whose authorization was raised in February, May and October 2026, and the October 2026 redemption in full of the remaining 569 of 2027 notes; this is a subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. The credit agreement dated March 5, 2025, with a revolver of 4,000 and a term loan, is described in the 2026 filings without any amendment. The next scheduled note maturity on the debt register in CP-1 is the 2028 notes. Terms of the agreements are Not supplied, so legal capacity, baskets and covenants are not assessed here.
## Calculations

No new calculation. Every figure is quoted from a located chunk or carried from CP-1 with the same value, period and unit. Where a share is stated (57% of FY2025 external revenues) it is printed in the 10-K FY2025 (page:13), not computed.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |
| Proxy statement not supplied: board, beneficial owners, control rights, executive pay and clawback | Medium | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the proxy statement referenced by Part III of the 10-K |
| Magellan Health sale agreement: buyer, price, closing conditions and proceeds not supplied | Medium | CP-2 | Supply the agreement or its 8-K |
| Receivable purchase agreement and performance guaranty not supplied; repurchase triggers unknown | Medium | CP-2 | Supply Exhibits 2.1 and 2.2 |

| Credit agreement and indentures not supplied; covenant definitions, baskets, guarantors and restricted payment capacity unknown | High for legal and covenant work | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply executed documents |
| Outcomes of Texas and Georgia protests and Arizona rebid not supplied | Medium | CP-2 | Supply later disclosures |
| Common dividend policy not located | Low | CP-2 | Confirm in the full 10-K or proxy |
| Events after October 27, 2026 not supplied | Medium | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply later 8-Ks |
| Releases duplicate the filings; no investor presentation, rating report or market data | Low | CP-2 | Not required for this scope |
## Next module

- CP-2: use the segment and state concentration, dated regulatory headwinds and the front-loaded earnings pattern as business-risk drivers alongside CP-1 figures; treat the sponsor as none; carry the receivable-agreement and covenant-definition gaps; do not infer creditor-adverse or supportive intent beyond the documented actions.

- CP-5: trace each row to its locator; check that figures match CP-1 exactly (total debt 15,542; unregulated cash available for general corporate use 175; revolver 4,000; debt to capital 41.1%; net receivable sale proceeds 970); keep the subsequent and future-dated labels; keep Management Language rows labelled.

## Findings

The view is adequate and improving, not yet secure. | Medium | Covenant definitions, guarantors and the receivable purchase agreement are not supplied, and the issuer reports no EBITDA, so leverage rests on an analyst definition. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt fell to USD 15,542 million from USD 17,401 million, and calculated leverage is 3.62x against 6.86x for FY2025. | Leverage has returned toward the FY2024 level, easing refinancing and debt service pressure. | Medium |

| Calculated EBITDA was USD 2,568 million in Q1 2026 and USD 325 million in Q3 2026. | The last-twelve-month ratios flatter the run rate, so fourth quarter results decide whether the improvement holds. | Medium |

| Cash available for general corporate use was USD 175 million, with an undrawn revolver of USD 4,000 million. | Parent liquidity depends on the revolver and subsidiary dividends, not on headline cash that is mostly regulated. | High |

| Government payors set rates and contracts, with state concentration and dated 2027 and 2028 regulatory changes. | Revenue visibility and margin depend on rate adequacy and procurement outcomes in a few states. | Medium |
### Credit view

Centene is a large, government-funded health insurer whose credit quality improved in 2026 but remains sensitive to medical costs and regulation. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt fell to USD 15,542 million from USD 17,401 million, calculated leverage on last-twelve-month EBITDA is 3.62x against 6.86x for FY2025, and a USD 4,000 million revolver is undrawn. The weakest point is earnings stability and parent-level cash: calculated EBITDA was USD 2,568 million in Q1 2026 but USD 325 million in Q3 2026, and cash available for general corporate use was USD 175 million. What decides the outcome is whether the health benefits ratio holds through the fourth quarter and the 2027 rate cycle while Marketplace, Medicaid and Star Ratings changes take effect.
### Credit assessment
| Item | View | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Overall fundamental credit view | Adequate and improving; sensitive to medical cost trend, state rate setting and regulation | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 Financials and credit metrics, Chart data: leverage; CP-1A Company and operating model, Credit translations |

| Business risk | Elevated: payors set premium, revenue is concentrated in government programs and a few states, and 2027 and 2028 changes are dated | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A Company and operating model (Revenue model, Segment mix, Concentration, Contract renewal risk, Regulatory calendar) |

| Financial risk | Moderate after deleveraging, with USD 15,542 million of debt, 3.62x calculated leverage and 6.85x cover of cash interest, but on an analyst-defined EBITDA | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; Chart data: leverage; Chart data: interest cover |

| Liquidity | Adequate at the parent through the USD 4,000 million undrawn revolver maturing March 5, 2030, with only USD 175 million of cash available for general corporate use | Documentary Fact | High | CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026; Chart data: liquidity |

| Governance and creditor control | No sponsor; documented actions are creditor-supportive; legal capacity under the indentures and credit agreement is not assessed | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour; Ownership, control and economic interest |

Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): Centene has repaired its balance sheet faster than its earnings are proven, so the credit is improving but depends on a stable health benefits ratio and on rate and regulatory outcomes that are outside its control. Basis: CP-1 leverage and quarterly EBITDA shape; CP-1A Credit translations.
### Key findings

First, Centene has reduced debt materially: total debt was USD 15,542 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 17,401 million at December 31, 2025, the 2027 notes, carried at USD 2,211 million at year-end, fell to USD 568 million at September 30, 2026, and the remainder was redeemed in October 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Debt register, Chart data: debt maturities; CP-1A Timeline). The mechanism is note repurchases funded by cash and by a USD 970 million receivable sale, and the implication is that no scheduled note maturity falls before 2028 on the CP-1 register.

Second, leverage looks sound on last-twelve-month figures but less so on the quarterly shape. Calculated total debt over EBITDA is 3.62x, against 2.98x for FY2024 and 6.86x for FY2025, and EBITDA over cash interest paid is 6.85x (Analyst Interpretation on an analyst-defined EBITDA; CP-1 Chart data: leverage and interest cover). Calculated EBITDA was USD 2,568 million in Q1 2026, USD 1,933 million in Q2 2026 and USD 325 million in Q3 2026, and Medicare Advantage earnings are front-loaded by the issuer's own account (Management Language; CP-1A Company and operating model, Seasonality). A creditor should therefore treat 3.62x as a ceiling on comfort until fourth quarter results confirm the recovery.

Third, parent liquidity is the binding constraint. Consolidated cash of USD 20,700 million sits mostly in regulated subsidiaries, unregulated cash is USD 376 million, and USD 175 million is available for general corporate use; management expects only about USD 20 million of net insurance-subsidiary dividends for the rest of 2026 (Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026; CP-1A Company and operating model, Subsidiary dividends). Debt service therefore rests on the undrawn USD 4,000 million revolver and on dividend capacity that state regulators control, with interest paid of USD 627 million over the last twelve months.

Fourth, reported cash flow overstates recurring generation. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 4,287 million includes net receivable sale proceeds of USD 970 million, and Q3 2026 operating cash flow was an outflow as state pass-through payments were paid through (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Reported cash flows, Narrative review). Free cash flow of USD 3,943 million over the last twelve months should not be read as a recurring figure.

Fifth, business risk is driven by government payors and dated regulatory change. Medicaid was 57% of FY2025 external revenues, Florida and New York each exceed about 10% of Medicaid premium revenues, certain Hawaii Medicaid contracts and the Florida Children's Medical Services contract were lost, and Texas and Georgia protests are open (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model, Concentration and Contract renewal risk). Marketplace membership fell to 3,403,300 from 5,828,100, 2027 Star Ratings cover about 42% of Medicare Advantage membership at 3.5 stars or higher against about 60%, and California and Medicaid work-requirement changes take effect in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Timeline, Credit translations). Revenue and margin visibility into 2027 and 2028 is therefore lower than the 2026 recovery suggests.

Sixth, the covenant has wide stated room but cannot be verified. Issuer debt to capital is 41.1% against a 0.60 to 1.00 maximum, and the issuer states compliance (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Covenants as disclosed), but the agreement's definition, guarantors and any restrictions on distributions are not supplied, so covenant headroom is Not calculable and legal capacity is not assessed (Insufficient Information).
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Scale and diversification across Medicaid, Medicare, Commercial and Other, with Medicaid in 30 states and Medicare Advantage in 32 states, spreads exposure across many payors even though two states are material (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company profile, Company and operating model). Deleveraging is real and documented: debt of USD 15,542 million, debt to capital of 41.1% against 46.5% at December 31, 2025, and the 2027 notes cleared (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Reported balance sheet, Debt register). Liquidity at the parent is supported by an undrawn USD 4,000 million revolver with no letters of credit against it, maturing March 5, 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026). Interest cover has recovered to 6.85x from 3.92x on an analyst-defined EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Chart data: interest cover). Documented management behaviour is creditor-supportive, with note repurchases, no common stock repurchases in Q3 2026, no sponsor and no documented value extraction (Analyst Interpretation on documented actions; CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour). The medical cost position improved on a nine-month basis, with a health benefits ratio of 89.9% against 91.1% a year earlier (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Credit translations).

Weaknesses. Earnings are volatile and front-loaded: calculated EBITDA fell to USD 2,535 million in FY2025 from USD 6,213 million in FY2024, and was USD 325 million in Q3 2026 (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics, Narrative review). Parent cash is thin relative to USD 15,542 million of debt, and upstream dividends are regulator-controlled (Documentary Fact; CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026). The business depends on government rate setting and procurement, with dated headwinds in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model, Timeline). Cash flow is distorted by pass-through timing and a receivable sale that carries repurchase obligations under the agreement, which is not supplied (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information; CP-1A Conflicts logged). Documentation gaps limit the view: covenant definitions, indentures, guarantors and the Magellan sale agreement are Not supplied (Insufficient Information). A Securities Action alleging false statements about 2025 guidance is pending, with no loss estimate and accrued amounts described as not material (Management Language; CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Category | Basis |

| Medical cost trend and health benefits ratio drift | Premium is fixed for the year while medical costs dominate cost; a small ratio change removes most margin, and Medicare costs rise through the year | EBITDA and cash interest cover can fall quickly, as FY2025 showed, pressuring leverage and covenant room | Material | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 Narrative review, Chart data: leverage; CP-1A Company and operating model |

| Regulatory and eligibility change | Medicaid work requirements and funding changes, expired Marketplace subsidies, lower Star Ratings and the California transition reduce membership before rates adjust | Revenue and margin visibility weaken into 2027 and 2028; refinancing capacity depends on earnings stability | Material | Documentary Fact | CP-1A Company and operating model, Timeline, Credit translations |

| Parent liquidity and subsidiary dividend dependence | Regulated subsidiaries hold most cash and need state approval to pay dividends; management expects little upstream cash in Q4 2026 | Debt service depends on the revolver and on regulator decisions | Material | Documentary Fact | CP-1 Liquidity at September 30, 2026; CP-1A Company and operating model, Subsidiary dividends |

| Contract losses and procurement protests | Medicaid contracts are rebid, with Florida Children's Medical Services and Hawaii lost and Texas and Georgia protested | Loss of scale and fixed-cost leverage; outcomes of protests are Not supplied | Material | Documentary Fact | CP-1A Company and operating model, Contract renewal risk |

| Unverified covenant and guarantee terms | Covenant definitions, indenture terms and guarantors are not supplied | Headroom and structural ranking cannot be confirmed | Material | Insufficient Information | CP-1 Covenants as disclosed; CP-1A Gaps |

| Receivable sale contingent claims | The facility has specified repurchase obligations, and Part D receivables of USD 2,668 million remain eligible for sale | A repurchase event would draw on liquidity; terms are not supplied | Minor | Insufficient Information | CP-1 Claims and obligations outside the debt figure; CP-1A Conflicts logged |

| Litigation | Securities and derivative actions allege misstatements on 2025 guidance | Potential cash cost or distraction; no estimate is given | Minor | Management Language | CP-1A Governance and issuer behaviour |
## Calculations

No new calculation. Every figure is carried from CP-1 or CP-1A with the same value, period and unit. The leverage and cover ratios use the analyst-calculated EBITDA defined in CP-1 (earnings from operations plus investment and other income plus depreciation, amortization of acquired intangibles and impairment), because the issuer reports no EBITDA.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Executed credit agreement and indentures not supplied | Covenant headroom is Not calculable; guarantor structure and ranking are unknown | Financial risk, governance and creditor control | High | Supply executed documents |

| Issuer reports no EBITDA | Leverage and cover use an analyst definition and may differ from agency or lender definitions | Financial risk | Medium | Compare with issuer or agency definitions if supplied |
| Receivable purchase agreement not supplied | Repurchase triggers and recourse to liquidity are unknown | Liquidity | Medium | Supply the agreement and performance guaranty |
| Magellan Health sale terms not supplied | Proceeds, timing and perimeter effects are unknown | Business risk, liquidity | Medium | Supply the sale agreement |
| Proxy statement not supplied | Ownership, control rights and board oversight are not assessed | Governance | Medium | Supply the proxy statement |
| Outcomes of Texas, Georgia and Arizona procurements not supplied | Contract wins or losses change revenue | Business risk | Medium | Supply later disclosures |
| Cash flows are cumulative only | Discrete quarterly cash flow rests on subtraction in CP-1 | Cash flow quality | Low | Check against quarterly filings |
| Events after October 27, 2026 not supplied | Fourth quarter results and later events may change the view | All | Medium | Supply later filings |
| Readiness status: CP-1 and CP-1A are READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | The synthesis inherits their limits; confidence is below High | All | Medium | Resolve the gaps above |
| No ratings, market prices or peer data in the context | Agency views and market pricing are not used | Assessment | Low | Not required for this scope |
## Next module

- CP-5: trace each figure here to CP-1 or CP-1A (debt of USD 15,542 million, leverage of 3.62x, cover of 6.85x, USD 175 million available cash, USD 4,000 million revolver, debt to capital of 41.1%, USD 970 million receivable sale proceeds) and confirm that every claim states its limitation.
- Downstream modules that cover relative value, security selection or the committee's action bias are outside this scope.
